promise_band.headline: You Hear the Price Before We Get in the Truck
promise_band.body: Nobody should find out what a visit costs when the plumber is already standing in their kitchen. Estimates are free on quoted work — remodels, water and sewer line replacement, fixture replacement. If your job is a service call instead, we tell you that on the phone, with the number, before we dispatch anybody. Ask us. We would rather have the conversation now than argue about an invoice later.

signature_system.headline: One Crew, One Truck, One Bill
signature_system.intro: Most Miami plumbers can change a fixture. Far fewer can find the line under your slab, dig it up, fix it and close the concrete back — without handing you off to two other companies and three separate invoices.

blocks.title: We own the heavy equipment
blocks.body: Septic tank work, excavation and concrete removal are all handled in house. We do not sub-contract any of it, which is why the hole gets dug the same week you call and gets closed the same day it is repaired.

blocks.title: We look before we dig
blocks.body: State-of-the-art video inspection finds concealed damage inside your sewer line, and jetting equipment clears it properly rather than punching a hole through the blockage and calling it done. And because most Miami-Dade businesses must keep an up-to-date backflow preventer under County ordinance, our certified arm Backflow Bob, Inc. handles the test, the certification and most simple repairs in a single visit.

about_block.headline: The Same Family Since 1968
about_block.body: Bay Plumbing Company has been owned and operated by the same family for 57 years, out of the same shop at 3029 SW 28th Street. That is not a marketing line — it is the reason we still have the inventory, the fleet and the excavation equipment that most Miami plumbing outfits gave up on. We are centrally located to our customer base, we stock what we install, and we do not sub-contract the difficult work to somebody who was not here last year and may not be here next year.

seo_body.headline: Plumbers in Miami-Dade County
paragraphs: Miami is hard on plumbing in ways most of the country never deals with. The water table sits high, which is why so many properties south of the Trail still run on septic and why a failing drainfield here becomes a yard problem fast. The older housing stock through Coconut Grove, Coral Gables and South Miami is still full of cast iron sewer line laid before anybody was thinking about a sixty-year service life. And the County keeps a close eye on backflow, with an ordinance requiring most commercial property to hold an up-to-date preventer.

None of that is fixture work. It needs a camera to find, a jetter or an excavator to reach, and a shop that owns both rather than renting them. We have been doing exactly that from SW 28th Street since 1968 — repairing and replacing drainfields, pumping and rebuilding septic tanks and grease traps, cutting in city sewer connections, and testing backflow preventers, usually in fifteen to twenty minutes.

The rest of it we do too, of course. Leaks concealed and visible, on every type of pipe. Stoppages, wherever they are. Water heaters, fixtures, remodels and new construction rough-in. Estimates are free on quoted work, and if the job is a service call instead, you will hear that number on the phone.

faqs.a: Estimates are free for work more involved than a service call — remodeling, replacing water or sewer lines, replacing fixtures, and similar quoted work. A straightforward service call is billed as a service call. Ask us on the phone which one your job is and we will tell you the number before we dispatch anyone.

Yes. We have had plumbers on call 24 hours a day, 365 days a year since 1968. Because our trucks carry a large inventory of common materials, an after-hours call is usually fixed on the first visit rather than made safe and rebooked for the morning.

faqs.q: Do you sub-contract septic, excavation or concrete work?
faqs.a: No. We own the equipment and run the crews in house — septic tank work, excavation and concrete removal included. That is why we can dig, repair and close back up without waiting on another company's schedule or adding another company's invoice.

faqs.q: How long does backflow testing take?
faqs.a: In most cases Backflow Bob, Inc. — our certified backflow testing arm — completes a test in 15 to 20 minutes, with the equipment and materials on hand to handle most simple repairs during the same visit.

faqs.q: Does Miami-Dade County require a backflow preventer?
faqs.a: Most Miami-Dade County businesses are required by County ordinance to have an up-to-date backflow preventer installed, and the Water and Sewer Department may contact you directly to require an annual test. Some older buildings never had one fitted at all. If you are not sure what you have, call us and we will find out.

faqs.q: My drainfield is soggy. Is that an emergency?
faqs.a: It is not a wait-and-see. Even small septic problems caused by damage to the drainfield turn into big ones if they are left, and in Miami's water table they turn fast. We inspect, diagnose and carry out the repair or replacement ourselves, excavation included.
Yes. Bay Plumbing Co. is licensed under C.C. 6469 and insured under CFC057007. Both numbers are printed on our estimates and painted on the building at 3029 SW 28th Street.

faqs.q: Do you handle commercial as well as residential?
faqs.a: Both, plus industrial. We serve Miami-Dade's residential, commercial and industrial plumbing needs, and we work regularly with landlords and property managers running multiple units.
